Sports.title: Stop calling the Europa League a major trophy, it’s Europe’s version of the Championship
Sports.content:
Before anyone gets angry, humour me for just a second...

Ever wonder why Newcastle's long major trophy drought officially ended when they won the Carabao Cup in 2025 and not the Championship title in 2017?

5 Why are we talking about Newcastle? Bear with... Credit: Rex

You probably don't. That's because the answer is fairly obvious.

We can all agree the word 'major', loosely defined, means 'bigger or more significant than others'.

So winning English football's second tier has never met the threshold for a major trophy, because objectively speaking, there is a level above.

The same is true of every single second-tier competition in the world.

Oh, except one. The Europa League. Which even comes with the same prize of being promoted into the superior league.

It started with West Ham and the Conference League. Then Tottenham and the Europa League. Before we knew it, these were widely accepted as major trophies.

But here's another thing we can probably agree on: it would be weird for Spurs to get relegated, claim the Championship title, and then mock all the Premier League teams who didn't win a trophy.

Yet last year it was totally normal to hold the Europa League over trophyless Arsenal - who were too good to compete for it and got knocked out of the Champions League instead.

In my book, those two things are the same: bragging about winning a trophy that better teams are not eligible for - as a literal result of qualifying to compete at a higher level.

This is not about the quality of opposition. It is totally possible to get a really favourable run in the Carabao Cup and face tough teams in the Europa League.

5 We are faced with the prospect of another English team claiming the Europa League as a major trophy when Aston Villa take on Freiburg in Istanbul Credit: Getty

It might even be harder to win the Europa League one year. That is not the point.

The best teams in England compete in the Carabao Cup. Somebody has to go and eliminate Arsenal or Manchester City - whether they field a weakened team or not. Therefore, it is a major trophy.

This is not English football bias, either. In Turkey, I think Trabzonspor winning the Turkish Cup would be a major trophy success, for example.

It really is this simple: the best teams in Europe do not compete in the Europa League, and if they did, they would win it.

We all know that if Paris Saint-Germain or Bayern Munich suddenly rocked up, they would walk it. Just like if we put Arsenal or Manchester City in the Championship.

And that is why we need to stop calling the Europa League a major trophy. By definition, it is the second tier of Europe.

5 This is not what winning a major trophy looks like Credit: Getty

By the way, if we were to have the argument about quality, the gap between the Champions League and the Europa League is gigantic.

Aston Villa can win this thing with knockout victories over Lille, Bologna, Nottingham Forest and Freiburg in the final tonight, which is live on talkSPORT.

As of right now, those teams have an average league position of ninth. There is nothing major about this.

Major success should be reserved for winning the top cup and league competitions domestically or on the continent.

The record books can't have Champions League and Europa League wins treated equally.

By all means, celebrate winning the Europa League. Go nuts. Trophies are great. Especially if, as a club, you are punching above your weight. Consider me the semantics police, not the celebration police.

5 That said, an open-top bus parade felt a bit much Credit: Getty

But are we suddenly in a world where it is better to finish sixth and win an easier tournament, than to come second and end up with nothing? If your answer is yes, why does anyone try and finish above sixth?

I would go as far as saying that getting to the Champions League semi-finals is a higher-ranking achievement than winning the Europa League. Unless you think Aston Villa or Freiburg would have got there over Arsenal, Atletico Madrid, Bayern or PSG this season?

Full disclosure: I'm a Chelsea fan. It is, of course, a different level of joy to win the lesser European competitions depending on the size of your club.

And no, this is not bitterness about our imminent lack of any European football...

There might be some who argue we should define these successes based on who wins. If it's a really great achievement relative to your club, call it a major trophy.

Chelsea winning the Conference League? Not a major trophy. West Ham winning it? Sure. But that doesn't work.

5 This was a wonderful achievement for West Ham. It wasn't a major trophy, though... Credit: Getty

Lincoln City were not expected to be anywhere near the top of League One at the start of this season. Is that suddenly a major trophy because they came first over Cardiff?

These are both third-tier competitions we're talking about, and yet nobody in their right mind would make that argument.

However, it's a European final and Villa's first since they beat Bayern to win the European Cup in 1982 and should they win the trophy - live on talkSPORT - it should be a spectacular occasion.

Just stop calling it a major one.

Sports.title: 75 percent of Americans don’t know who Mauricio Pochettino is as World Cup faces urgent USA challenge
Sports.content:
The World Cup has a big problem in the USA if 75 percent of American adults don't know who USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino is and hotels are struggling to fill rooms.

75 percent of Americans don’t know who Mauricio Pochettino is as World Cup faces urgent USA challenge

Overpriced tickets and international travel issues have shadowed the biggest sports tournament in history for months.

But one of FIFA's largest hurdles during the 2026 World Cup could be overall awareness in the United States, which will be the main home of the two-month tournament and contains 11 host cities including Los Angeles, Atlanta and New York/New Jersey.

5 Mauricio Pochettino is set to lead the USMNT at the 2026 FIFA World Cup Credit: Getty

Pochettino isn't a household name in USA

While Mauricio Pochettino zeroes in on a May 26 announcement for his final United States Men's National Team roster, it's fair to ask how many Americans -- soccer diehards and normal sport followers -- even know who the USMNT coach is.

A recent survey of 1,000 American adults by SeatPick revealed a stunning lack of awareness about USA men's soccer and the looming World Cup, which will feature 104 matches spread among the United States, Mexico and Canada.

According to the survey, 76.1 percent of US adults didn't know who Pochettino is, while only 12.6 percent accurately identified the former Tottenham, Chelsea and PSG coach as the current leader of USMNT.

Some responded by asserting that Pochettino was either a former NFL quarterback, South American president, Michelin-starred chef or an animal in a children's cartoon.

With the cheapest remaining official in-stadium tickets for the July 19 World Cup final priced at a whopping $35,000 -- a ticket for an 'exclusive retreat located in our secure perimeter immediately outside the stadium' costs $16,475 -- there have been lingering accusations by football fans across the globe of price gouging and unconstrained World Cup capitalism.

"I did not know that number," US President Donald Trump told The New York Post, when asked about the prohibitive cost of World Cup tickets.

"I would certainly like to be there, but I wouldn't pay it either, to be honest with you."

With the countdown clock at 22 days and ticking, another looming question is when a true World Cup buzz will take over America.

Is World Cup fever connecting with US fans?

According to the survey, San Antonio, Las Vegas, Indianapolis and Denver were the most 'unaware' cities in the country when asked about the World Cup being hosted in the USA.

"These numbers should be a wake-up call for tournament organisers," SeatPick CEO Gilad Zilberman said.

5 More than 75 percent of Americans don't know who Mauricio Pochettino is, according to a recent survey Credit: getty

5 Christian Pulisic can make his name in the USA with a massive World Cup run Credit: getty

"You can sell tickets to the most engaged fans, but if three-quarters of the host country can't identify the national team's coach, the mainstream audience is still to be won. The cities with the biggest awareness gaps are exactly the markets that need targeted outreach before the summer."

A USMNT squad expected to feature Christian Pulisic, Chris Richards and Tyler Adams will open World Cup Group Stage play on June 12 vs Paraguay at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.

Dallas was listed in the survey as the 'most aware' city about the US hosting the 2026 World Cup, while 20 combined matches will be played in two Texas cities.

Chris Canetti, president of the Houston World Cup Host Committee, said that strong final ticket sales are expected at NRG Stadium, which will host seven matches and twice feature Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.

Even with high prices, sell outs will happen

"We don't get too much of the ticket data, believe it or not," Canetti exclusively told talkSPORT.

"FIFA controls all the ticketing. But from the limited data we get or see, we do expect all the games to be sold out here.

"There are some limited tickets available right now to the matches here in Houston. We got a very good draw with three of the top 10 teams in the world in Portugal, the Netherlands and Germany.

"We have two knockout games -- two knockout round games that project, if the seedings hold, one would be Brazil versus Japan. The other one would be the Netherlands coming back to play Morocco. So we'll see if that happens.

"But we also have three teams making their World Cup debuts in Cape Verde, Uzbekistan, and Curacao. There's a lot of interest from those countries, so we're lucky. Ticket sales are moving here."

NBA playoffs and hotel problems also cause concern

The real concern is the remainder of a huge country that normally is devoted to the NFL, college football and a variety of sports in a loaded calendar that never stops.

The peak of the NBA playoffs will also split time with the World Cup, as a league showcasing Victor Wembanyama, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Brunson won't begin its final postseason round until June 3.

England faces Croatia on June 17 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, while Game 7 of the NBA Finals could be played on June 19.

5 Victor Wembanyama is more popular than USMNT's best players Credit: getty

5 Cristiano Ronaldo is still very much the heartbeat of the Portugal squad Credit: getty

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has regularly hyped the majesty of the 2026 World Cup and stood behind the high ticket prices.

"It will be a fantastic event. It will be 104 Super Bowls in one month,” Infantino exclusively told talkSPORT before Super Bowl LX.

"The world will stand still and observe the biggest global event that humanity has ever seen."

USMNT needs a big summer run to raise soccer awareness

While USA residents slowly figure out who coaches a team that's supposed to lift soccer to a new stage in America, another worrying sign has emerged.

A report from the American Hotel and Lodging Association, which surveyed more than 200 hotels among the 11 host US cities, found that almost 80 percent of hotel bookings are below initial projections.

"FIFA room block over commitment created an artificial early demand signal that has since unraveled, with roughly half of respondents in host markets reporting material room block releases. " the report stated.

"Many hotels indicate that early booking signals overstated true demand."

The 2026 World Cup is already the most expensive tournament in sports history.

The final payoff in the USA is a growing question mark, and it will take a scorching summer run from Pochettino's USMNT crew to change the current lack of awareness.

Sports.title: Man United told to make ruthless decision to sell injury prone £43m man
Sports.content:
Manchester United should offload £43million defender Matthijs de Ligt as part of the club’s summer squad shake-up.

That’s the view of the panel of talkSPORT’s dedicated Manchester United show titled Inside Devils.

3 Matthijs de Ligt has been missing since late November with a back injury Credit: Getty

The Dutch defender’s season came to an abrupt end in November after suffering a back injury.

The persistent issue hampered his hopes of a return to the first team but he was forced to go under the knife last week to resolve the issue.

Manchester United released a statement clarifying the situation, claiming the decision was made in the player's best interests after rehabilitation work failed to provide the expected results.

His recovery will see him miss this summer’s World Cup with the 26-year-old not expected back until ‘early next season’.

De Ligt has suffered with multiple injury layoffs since arriving at Old Trafford from Bayern Munich in 2024.

And as United prepare to embark on a new era with Michael Carrick set to take over on a permanent basis, De Ligt’s future at the club has been called into question.

Inside Devils panellists Angelina Kelly, Flex and Alex Crook all provided their opinion on whether the former Ajax captain should be retained as part of the club’s rebuild.

Brutal assessment

“I’m going to be ruthless here, I think the injury problems are too much. I don’t think you can carry a passenger,” talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook said.

“There were some signs before he got injured that he was starting to warm to the task of being a United player and finding his feet in the Premier League but I’d get rid because of the injury issues. Sorry."

Asked if she agreed with Crook’s take, Kelly replied: “I kind of do and I feel really sorry for De Ligt in a sense because his career has not gone the way I expected when he was that young kid captaining Ajax.

3 The Dutch defender underwent a recovery programme which failed to yield the required results Credit: Getty

“This isn’t the route I thought it would go and I think it is just down to the fitness side of it.

“I agree with Crook, I think he was starting to come into his own with Man United and he had some really good moments.

“But if the guy can’t stay fit, and he’s been out a long time, I don't know, I imagine he might stay for squad depth depending on what happens with this injury. But he’s not good enough."

Flex took a more sympathetic approach to the defender’s situation and while openly pinpointing the star’s attributes, he admits fearing for De Ligt’s future.

“I tend to agree but it’s down to availability. I think we’ve got big question marks over a lot of players,” Flex said.

“I think he’s a really good player, I really do. He was really strong before that injury but you’re just wondering is that going to be put behind him now.

3 De Ligt has been reduced to a mere spectator for the last six months Credit: Getty

“Clean summer, obviously not going to the World Cup. Finally got the surgery, he’s expected back early next season and even that is another risk isn’t it?

“That could be September or October so it doesn’t look like he’s even going to have a pre-season.

“It’s not looking good for him.”

De Ligt wrote an emotional message to fans after undergoing surgery but assured them that he would do all he could to come back stronger.

Writing on Instagram, De Ligt said: "After 6 months of treatment and working hard to get back, surgery was the only option left.

“I’m disappointed I couldn’t help the team the last 6 months and obviously missing out on the World Cup but I am looking forward to doing everything to get back in front of the fans and feeling better again."

Sports.title: What will Premier League’s sixth place get if Aston Villa win Europa League but finish fifth?
Sports.content:
What will Premier League’s sixth place get if Aston Villa win Europa League but finish fifth?

Aston Villa have the chance to claim European glory tonight when they face Freiburg in the Europa League final.

Villa, who smashed Liverpool last time out to boost their confidence ahead of the Istanbul showpiece, swept Nottingham Forest aside in the semi-finals.

2 Watkins scored Aston Villa's first on a memorable night of European action at Villa Park

Unai Emery's side sit fourth in the Premier League heading into the final day of the season this weekend but before that, are on the cusp of a first major piece of European silverware since 1982.

And the winner of the Europa League secures their spot in the Champions League, just as Tottenham managed last season.

However, with fifth place now enough to join Europe's elite club competition for the 2026-27 campaign, there are question marks over what happens if Villa win the Europa League and then finish fifth.

It was recently confirmed that the Premier League will be given a European Performance Spot in the Champions League as reward for English clubs' collective progress in European competition this season.

There will be a Premier League side in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League finals this season, with Arsenal and Crystal Palace joining Villa in their pursuit of continental silverware.

Teams currently in sixth, though, will be playing close attention to Villa's run in and their looming clash with Freiburg.

That's because if Villa end up finishing fifth but win the Europa League, the Premier League will earn an additional Champions League spot.

As things stand, Bournemouth on 56 points would earn a place in the competition next season.

The Cherries face competition from below, however, with Brighton three points off their fellow south coast side but with a superior goal difference.

Bournemouth take on Forest in Sunday's top-flight finale while Brighton host Manchester United.

2 Emery is looking to win the Europa League for the fifth time Credit: Getty

Conversely, should Villa hold on to fourth and win the Europa League, the Premier League won't be awarded an additional Champions League spot.

In this instance, the team that finishes sixth would then qualify for the Europa League regardless of Villa's European exploits.

Villa are currently three points clear of fifth-placed Liverpool ahead of the final matchday of the season this Sunday.

However, the Reds do have a better goal difference so it could yet be a grandstand finish.

Villa make the trip to Manchester City on Sunday, just a few days after what will be an emotional night in Turkey.

Liverpool host Brentford and should they win and Villa fail to, Arne Slot's side would finished fourth.
